frontmatter.title: Structural connectivity dMRI
frontmatter.description: Build a single-subject diffusion MRI structural connectome with MRtrix3 in Neurodesk.

children.value: By the end of this tutorial you will be able to:
Prepare anatomical and diffusion inputs from the HCP 100307 example.
Run an MRtrix3 tractography and connectome workflow in Neurodesk.

This example follows one HCP subject through a standard MRtrix3 workflow. It uses 100,000 streamlines so the example is practical to run; increase that number only when you have enough time and storage for a larger tractogram.

, either through Neurodesk Play or a local Neurodesktop installation. Use a desktop terminal for the processing commands and MRview for the image checks. The screenshots were captured from native desktop windows in Neurodesk Play using MRtrix3 3.0.3, FSL 6.0.5.1 and FreeSurfer 7.4.1.

children.value: MRtrix reads the compressed NIfTI directly, so there is no need to expand
into a multi-gigabyte file. Convert the image and import its FSL gradient table:

mrconvert ../T1w/Diffusion/data.nii.gz DWI.mif \
  -fslgrad ../T1w/Diffusion/bvecs ../T1w/Diffusion/bvals \
  -datatype float32 -stride 0,0,0,1

dwibiascorrect ants DWI.mif DWI_bias.mif -bias bias.mif
dwi2response dhollander DWI_bias.mif response_wm.txt response_gm.txt response_csf.txt

prints the voxel selection it used for each tissue before writing the three response-function files. The Neurodesk MRtrix3 container already includes the ANTs and FSL commands that these scripts call, so no extra modules are needed.

children.alt: Terminal output at the end of dwi2response, listing the refined CSF, GM and single-fibre WM voxel selections

children.value: Estimate the fibre orientation distributions (FODs) with multi-shell multi-tissue CSD and normalise them:

dwi2mask DWI_bias.mif DWI_mask.mif
dwi2fod msmt_csd DWI_bias.mif \
  response_wm.txt wmfod.mif response_gm.txt gm.mif response_csf.txt csf.mif \
  -mask DWI_mask.mif
mtnormalise wmfod.mif wmfod_norm.mif gm.mif gm_norm.mif csf.mif csf_norm.mif \
  -mask DWI_mask.mif

children.alt: Terminal showing dwi2mask, dwi2fod for four shells and three tissues, and mtnormalise completing

children.value: Create a five-tissue-type (5TT) image from the brain-extracted T1w image, then register its grey-matter volume to the diffusion mean b=0 image. The transform will later align both the 5TT image and the parcellation with diffusion space.

5ttgen fsl ../T1w/T1w_acpc_dc_restore_brain.nii.gz 5TT.mif -premasked
dwiextract DWI_bias.mif - -bzero | mrmath - mean mean_b0.mif -axis 3
mrconvert mean_b0.mif mean_b0.nii.gz
mrconvert 5TT.mif 5TT.nii.gz
fslroi 5TT.nii.gz 5TT_gm.nii.gz 0 1
flirt -in mean_b0.nii.gz -ref 5TT_gm.nii.gz -dof 6 -omat diff2struct_fsl.mat
transformconvert diff2struct_fsl.mat mean_b0.nii.gz 5TT_gm.nii.gz \
  flirt_import diff2struct_mrtrix.txt
mrtransform 5TT.mif -linear diff2struct_mrtrix.txt -inverse 5TT_coreg.mif
5tt2gmwmi 5TT_coreg.mif gmwmSeed_coreg.mif
runs FSL’s FAST and FIRST inside the MRtrix3 container and takes roughly 15–20 minutes; the remaining commands finish in seconds.

children.alt: Terminal showing the end of 5ttgen followed by the b=0 extraction, FLIRT registration, transform conversion and 5tt2gmwmi commands

children.value: Generate a 100,000-streamline iFOD2 tractogram using grey–white matter interface seeding and anatomical constraints, then estimate a SIFT2 weight for each streamline:

tckgen wmfod_norm.mif tracks_100k.tck \
  -algorithm iFOD2 -act 5TT_coreg.mif -backtrack -crop_at_gmwmi \
  -seed_gmwmi gmwmSeed_coreg.mif -maxlength 300 -select 100000 -nthreads 4

tcksift2 tracks_100k.tck wmfod_norm.mif sift2_weights.txt \
  -act 5TT_coreg.mif -out_mu sift2_mu.txt -nthreads 4
reports how many seeds and streamlines it needed to select 100,000 that satisfy the anatomical constraints; with four threads it took about six minutes in the run shown.
then prints its optimisation summary and writes one weight per streamline.

children.alt: Terminal showing tckgen selecting 100,000 streamlines and tcksift2 finishing its optimisation

children.value: 4. Generate the parcellation and build the connectome

children.label: 4. Generate the parcellation and build the connectome

children.value: The original example used a precomputed FreeSurfer
image. Here we generate labels from the supplied T1w image with
option adds Desikan–Killiany cortical regions to the subcortical segmentation. This is a volumetric neural-network parcellation, not the surface-based
pipeline, so its labels and connectivity values will differ from the original HCP reconstruction.
Run this in the same Neurodesktop terminal, from

ml freesurfer/7.4.1
mri_synthseg --i ../T1w/T1w_acpc_dc_restore_brain.nii.gz \
  --o parcellation_synthseg.nii.gz --parc --cpu --threads 8 \
  --qc synthseg_qc.csv
ml mrtrix3/3.0.3 fsl/6.0.5.1

SynthSeg internally resamples the input to 1 mm resolution while retaining its anatomical world coordinates. Check the resulting parcellation against the anatomy before continuing; in MRview, scroll through the brain and use the Overlay tool’s visibility checkbox to compare the labels with the underlying image:
The QC CSV is an additional automated check; visual inspection remains necessary. Close each MRview window when you have finished checking it to return to the terminal. Use
(F2) to inspect all three planes. Allow several minutes for CPU inference and extra time for a module’s first launch.
Convert the Desikan–Killiany parcellation to MRtrix node labels, transform it into diffusion space, and build a symmetric, SIFT2-weighted matrix.
needs two lookup tables: the FreeSurfer colour table, which is not part of the MRtrix3 container, and the MRtrix3
ordering, which is. Download the FreeSurfer table into the results folder first; the MRtrix3 path below is valid inside the Neurodesk

curl -fsSL -o FreeSurferColorLUT.txt \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/freesurfer/freesurfer/v7.2.0/distribution/FreeSurferColorLUT.txt
FREESURFER_LUT=FreeSurferColorLUT.txt
MRTRIX_LUT=/opt/mrtrix3-3.0.3/share/mrtrix3/labelconvert/fs_default.txt

labelconvert parcellation_synthseg.nii.gz \
  "$FREESURFER_LUT" "$MRTRIX_LUT" nodes.mif
mrtransform nodes.mif -linear diff2struct_mrtrix.txt -inverse \
  -datatype uint32 nodes_coreg.mif
tck2connectome tracks_100k.tck nodes_coreg.mif connectome.csv \
  -tck_weights_in sift2_weights.txt -symmetric -zero_diagonal \
  -scale_invnodevol -out_assignments assignments.txt

children.alt: Terminal showing labelconvert, mrtransform and tck2connectome producing connectome.csv

children.value: is an 84 × 84 matrix (34 cortical regions per hemisphere plus the subcortical structures in

, then paste the following). The figure opens as a desktop window:

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

connectome = np.loadtxt('connectome.csv', delimiter=',')
plt.figure(figsize=(7, 6))
plt.imshow(connectome, cmap='viridis')
plt.colorbar(label='SIFT2 weight / node volume')
plt.title('HCP 100307 SIFT2-weighted connectome')
plt.xlabel('Region')
plt.ylabel('Region')
plt.show()
